# RedKinNet <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/PaoloDalena/RedKinNet/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PaoloDalena/RedKinNet/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

RedKinNet selects sets of unrelated individuals from pairwise kinship estimates, such as
those of KING or PLINK 2. Pairs related above a threshold form a network whose connected
components, the families, are resolved exactly, so that the selection is always as large as
possible, also in the large and intricate families of genetic isolates. Among the many
selections of the largest size, RedKinNet can draw one uniformly at random, with the exact
probability that each individual is selected; choose by preferences for individuals; or
reach a target proportion or mean of a covariate over the whole selection.

## Installation

You can install the development version of RedKinNet from GitHub with:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("PaoloDalena/RedKinNet")
```

## Example

The package includes `rkn_example`, a synthetic cohort with a kinship table and covariates.

```{r example}
library(RedKinNet)

# Check the samples: duplicates and possible contamination
chk <- rkn_check_samples(rkn_example$kinship, threshold = "third",
                         samples = rkn_example$samples$id)

# The network of relatives up to the third degree, without the contaminated sample
g <- rkn_graph_from_kinship(rkn_example$kinship, threshold = "third",
                            samples = rkn_example$samples$id,
                            exclude = chk$contamination$id,
                            covariates = rkn_example$samples, check = FALSE)

# A largest set of unrelated individuals, drawn uniformly among all of them
sel <- rkn_select_random(g, uniform = TRUE, seed = 1)
sel

# A largest set with half women
rkn_select_global(g, "sex", target = c(F = 0.5), seed = 1)
```

## Features

- **Exact maximum sets**: every family is resolved by an exact algorithm, with a reduction
  that keeps intricate families tractable.
- **Selection uncertainty**: uniform draws among all the largest selections, their number,
  and the exact inclusion probability of every individual.
- **Preferences**: criteria on covariates, such as a minimum call rate or the age at onset
  of a disease, decide among the largest selections of each family.
- **Composition targets**: a target proportion or mean of a covariate over the whole
  selection, reached exactly by choosing all the families jointly, with the trade-off
  between selection size and composition.
- **Sample checks**: possible duplicates, contaminated samples and samples of different
  ancestry are flagged before selecting.
- **Diagnostics**: every decision is recorded and can be summarised and plotted.
